- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70→75+), then fail to correct downward.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — model holds high forecasts too long after price drops.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price declines; often takes 3–5 days to adjust downward.
- Forecasts for 30d horizon show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when recent history includes strong upward momentum.
- When true outcome shows sharp downward trend, model fails to reduce forecast early; overcorrects later.
- Model underestimates volatility in early periods, leading to overly optimistic mid-term forecasts.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture sudden reversals or short-term volatility spikes.
- Model tends to ignore recent low prices in the 30d history when forecasting, leading to persistent overestimation.
- When true price drops below 65–70, model often fails to adjust forecast downward until 7–10 days later.
